summary: Repository-local organization policy, verification and contract-discovery commands; not installed shared runtime dependencies.

provides.name: local-verification
provides.summary: Discover maintained root and skill test locations, run isolated unittest processes, report skips, validate the registry, and check an existing development installation without refreshing it.

provides.name: architecture-check
provides.summary: CLEAN checks for declared runtime/test separation, shared-runtime independence from skill imports, and the explicit orchestrator workflow/domain dependency allow-list. Components cannot import the controller; domain rules and runtime consumers cannot import the state compatibility facade; the declared allow-list is checked for cycles. Literal _load_component calls are included; computed loading still needs review.

provides.name: implemented-contract-registry
provides.summary: Validate v1 subsystem records, local paths, and plan-qualified stable IDs (with legacy string support); --write-index regenerates the discovery router only when records validate.

artifacts.name: repository-code-organization-policy
artifacts.summary: Project-owned policy governs new/materially changed production, test, eval, fixture and harness assets: responsibility placement, module encapsulation, decisions/effects, state/rule ownership, dependency direction, proportionate functions/classes, coherent transactions, verification ownership, module documentation and accumulated growth. Explain owner/placement/dependencies before structural additions or material growth and concrete exceptions; return unresolved material architecture/scope decisions to the owner. Mandatory rules govern introduced/materially worsened structure; metrics remain advisory, untouched debt stays outside scope and no review stage is added. Maps describe current ownership. The development installer ships consumers, not this project policy.

invariants.statement: Default verification neither installs dependencies nor runs live model evals. Passing with reported skips does not qualify skipped capabilities.
Subsystem JSON records are editable current-state routing; index.json is generated. Schemas, code and tests remain underlying authority.
Architecture rules are deterministic constraints; complexity measurements remain advisory and are not acceptance thresholds.
